measurement: where a defect's released block actually goes: parked in Zend's per-size-class cache, or passed to libc free(). A property of the defect's release, measured in the allocator, not read off a sanitizer's output
not_an_arm: this record gives no case a verdict and declares no arm. It is a side measurement in the sense of SCHEMA.md rule 6: matrix.tsv, inputs.json and a README, no captures

platform.host: x86_64 Linux, the project's own machine; not the machine this corpus's own populations were measured on (that one is gcc 15.2 / libasan 15)

probe.what: stock allocator (cache ON, REAL_SIZE unpatched) with the release probe

locator.what: the source corpus's detector patches (ZEND_DISABLE_MEMORY_CACHE 1, REAL_SIZE unrounded) under ASan; used ONLY to name the block and to prove the trigger reaches the use

decisive.what: stock cache ON, probe in, ASan on, in ONE binary: ASan can only report a use-after-free on a block that reached libc, and the probe says at the same address in the same run what happened to it
decisive.cflags: same as locator, without the detector patches

probe: four emit points in Zend/zend_alloc.c: the cache branch of _efree (CACHED), its fall-through to ZEND_DO_FREE (FREED), _erealloc (REALLOC, which never consults the cache), the cache drain at request shutdown (DRAINED) and the shutdown leak sweep (SWEPT). ZEND_DO_FREE is plain free() on this build: ZEND_MM is not defined

controls.size_ceiling: a payload of 81 bytes or more is never cached: 0 of 170 in the control run, which is what cache_index = ((size+7)&~7)>>3 < MAX_CACHED_MEMORY (11) predicts from the source
controls.cache_fills: a payload of 80 or less goes both ways, 2729 cached against 790 passed through, which is the 256-entry per-class cache filling and falling back to free()
controls.survives_a_crash: the probe writes unbuffered; a run that dies with a signal still leaves its log (814 lines on the crashing control)
controls.silent_when_off: with ZPROBE_OUT unset the build writes nothing and is the stock allocator
controls.untested_branch: SWEPT, the shutdown leak sweep, did not fire in any control and is reported as unproven. The three nested-until-teardown cases rest on DRAINED, which does fire

cross_check: the two instruments agree on every case they both see: 17 of 17 where ASan named a block and the probe had a record for it, 0 disagreements. The 2 they do not are the answer for those 2, the blocks that never passed through Zend's allocator at all, and they are exactly the 2 cases plain-temporal-repros independently records as its only nested=false entries
found_by_the_cross_check: three cases first read as parked while ASan reported a use-after-free on them. The probe was missing the cache drain at request shutdown; instrumenting it brought the disagreements to zero and separated nested-until-teardown as its own class
build_deviations: configure's AC_PROG_LEX probe needs a lex this host does not have; the cached config from the corpus's own configured tree carries the answer and PHP 5.0.0 ships its generated scanners
the generated Makefile's EXTRA_LIBS omits -ldl for the sanitised link; it is supplied on the make command line
not_committed: the per-case probe logs and ASan reports are captures and stay out of the repo (SCHEMA.md rule 6). matrix.tsv is the summary
